[[File:Guy Kargl portrait.jpg|thumb|right|260px]]
'''Guy Kargl''' ([[Players Committee]] forum handle '''Freelancer''') won Decipher's 1997 Design a Card contest. His design became the [[Special Edition]] Effect [[S-foils]]. He was a 28-year-old hardware and software design engineer and a sanctioned tournament director from Tulsa, Oklahoma.<ref name="linkedin-kargl">[https://www.linkedin.com/in/guy-kargl-eet-pmp-67a2835/ Guy Kargl, EET, PMP], LinkedIn profile, 1 November 2026 (Experience: "Senior Design Engineer, XETA Technologies, Inc, May 1993 – Jul 2006", Broken Arrow, OK; "Assisted in creating a telephone switch (also known as a PBX) system"; "Designed Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs)"; "Wrote Software in Dataflex, HTML, and C"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101104014/https://swccg.com/snapshots/linkedin/guy-kargl.html Internet Archive]</ref> He had played the [[Star Wars CCG]] since its November 1995 launch.<ref name="win">[http://www.decipher.com/insidedecipher/archives/1997/designawinner.html Guy Kargl Wins Star Wars CCG Card Design Contest], Rich Loftus, Decipher (23 May 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990210055006/http://www.decipher.com/insidedecipher/archives/1997/designawinner.html Internet Archive]</ref> He was Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]] Red 61 FL from Tulsa. His slot was marked Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.<ref name="smlist" /> He was a call-in guest on [[Radio Free Decipher]] broadcast 9 (26 February 1999) with Chris Swearingen, [[Alex Alcalde]] and [[Carl Mike Hardy|Mike Hardy]].<ref name="rfd-09">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QU24jFxZsHM Radio Free Decipher 09], Player's Council (26 February 1999). Guests Chris Swearingen, [[Alex Alcalde]], Mike Hardy, and [[Guy Kargl]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-QU24jFxZsHM Internet Archive].</ref>

In July and August 2003 he organized the Vintage Stock Tour, seven [[Sealed Deck]] tournaments for Star Wars CCG and [[Young Jedi]], one a weekend from 12 July to 30 August 2003 at Vintage Stock stores in Oklahoma, Arkansas, Kansas and Missouri, with uncut sheets from the Players Committee given away at random at each event.<ref name="pcf-1895-30301">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=30301#30301 Vintage Stock Tour! Uncut Sheet Prizes! 7 tournaments!], Guy Kargl, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (4 July 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041101152255/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=30301 Internet Archive]</ref> He ran four of the events himself, with [[John McDaniel]] running one and [[Vicki Luthy]] two.<ref name="pcf-1895-30304">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=30304#30304 Vintage Stock Tour! Uncut Sheet Prizes! 7 tournaments!], Guy Kargl, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (4 July 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041101152255/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=30301 Internet Archive]</ref> At the Star Wars CCG event in Tulsa on 26 July 2003, played mostly with Death Star II cards, he finished 6th of eight with the Dark Side.<ref name="pcf-1895-31138">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=31138#31138 Vintage Stock Tour! Uncut Sheet Prizes! 7 tournaments!], Guy Kargl, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (30 July 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041101152255/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=30301 Internet Archive]</ref> He was the tournament director of the 2004 Oklahoma State Championship, held on 24 July 2004 at the All Star Sports Complex in Tulsa.<ref name="pcf-3537-48346">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=48346#48346 2004 Oklahoma State Championship -- July 24, 2004], Guy Kargl, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (30 June 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040901021342/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=51176%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>
